grammar_focus: suggest/insist/demand that + (should) + 动词原形(虚拟语气)、be qualified to do / be subject to / be justified、固定短语 in the belief that / in writing / on one's behalf / in question / put an end to、形容词后置修饰名词(complaints large and small;the officer in question)、so … that / it is possible for sb to do(原创承载 NCE3 第三册 L53 考点·无需净化:公民制度科普——瑞典司法特派员(Ombudsman)保护公民不受专横或不称职官员欺压;Aaron 预警的“丑闻”属误判,实为公民制度说明文,仅把“虐待/粗暴/起诉”轻软化为“不公对待/更严肃处理”;保留瑞典史实背景,美式化拼写)
scene: 斯堪的纳维亚半岛各国实行的开明社会政策,受到全世界的推崇。在瑞典,已逐渐形成了一种完善的制度,用来保护每个公民不受专横或不称职的政府官员欺压。由于这种制度行之有效,已被其他国家采纳。是瑞典人最先认识到:政府工作人员——如文职人员、警官、卫生稽查员、税务人员等等——也会犯错误,或者自以为在为公众服务而把事情做过了头。早在 1809 年,瑞典议会就建立了一个保护公民利益的制度。议会内有一个代表各政党利益的委员会,由它委派一位称职的人专门调查个人对国家的意见。此人官衔为“司法特派员”,但瑞典人一般管他叫“J.O.”,即“司法特派员”。司法特派员不受任何政治压力的制约。他听取社会各阶层大大小小的意见,并进行调查。由于意见均须用书面形式提出,司法特派员每年平均收到 1,200 封信,他有 8 位律师做他的助手协助工作,每封信都详细批阅。司法特派员的工作没有什么秘密可言,他的来往信件是公开的、供公众监督。如果公民的意见正确,司法特派员便替他伸张正义。他采取的行动因意见的性质不同而有所不同:他可以温和地批评某位官员,也可以甚至向议会提议修改某项法律。下面这件事就是司法特派员工作的一个典型例子。一个住在瑞典乡村的外国人写信给司法特派员,抱怨说他仅仅因为是个外国人就受到一名警官的不公对待。司法特派员立即写信给当地的警察局长,请他寄来与此事有关的材料。材料中没有任何文字记载证明这个外国人所说的情况符合事实,警察局长也矢口否认这一指控。司法特派员一时无从下手。但是,当他又收到住在同一村庄的另一个外国人写来的一封内容类似的投诉信时,他立即派出一位律师前去调查。律师查实:那名警官确实多次不公地对待外国人。可是,这名警官对外国人抱有偏见这一事实,在官方档案中根本无法记载,司法特派员只有派他的代表去核对事实才能查明。当事的那名警官受到严厉批评,并被告知:如果再有针对他的投诉,他将受到更严肃的处理。司法特派员的果断行动,当即制止了一种若不然可能就无人察觉的不公做法。

grammar_card.title: suggest that + (should) + 原形 / be qualified to·be subject to / 固定短语 / 后置修饰 / so…that
grammar_card.intro: ①suggest/insist/demand/require that 后接的从句用 (should) + 动词原形(虚拟语气);被动为 (should) be done:suggest that a law be altered。②be qualified to do(胜任做)、be subject to(受…控制)、be justified(有正当理由)。③固定短语:in the belief that(自以为)、in writing(书面)、on one's behalf(代表某人)、in question(当事的)、put an end to(制止)。④意义相反的形容词并用时后置修饰名词:complaints large and small。⑤so … that(如此…以至于)、it is + 形容词 + for sb + to do(形式主语)。

be qualified to do / be subject to
qualified to investigate; not subject to pressure

specialRules.rule: suggest(建议)、insist(坚持)、demand(要求)后的 that 从句用(should)+ 动词原形,should 常省略;被动为(should)be done。
意义相反的两个形容词(large and small)并用修饰名词时,要放在被修饰词之后;in question 也放名词之后。
美式拼写:recognize(英式 recognise)、practice(英式动词 practise)、center(英式 centre)。本课已按美语写。

prelisten.q: Listen and answer — What could not be reported in the official files?
options: The fact that the officer was prejudiced against foreigners

passage: The Scandinavian countries are much admired all over the world for their enlightened social policies. Sweden has evolved an excellent system for protecting the individual citizen from high-handed or incompetent public officials. The system has worked so well that it has been adopted in other countries too. The Swedes were among the first to recognize that public officials such as civil servants, police officers, health inspectors, and tax collectors can make mistakes or act over-zealously in the belief that they are serving the public. As long ago as 1809, the Swedish Parliament introduced a plan to safeguard the interest of the individual. A parliamentary committee representing all political parties appoints a person who is suitably qualified to investigate private grievances against the State. The official title of this person is 'Justitieombudsman,' but the Swedes commonly refer to him as the 'J.O.' or 'Ombudsman.' The Ombudsman is not subject to political pressure. He investigates complaints large and small that come to him from all levels of society. Since complaints must be made in writing, the Ombudsman receives an average of twelve hundred letters a year, and he has eight legal assistants to help him examine every single one in detail. There is nothing secretive about the Ombudsman's work, for his correspondence is open to public inspection. If a citizen's complaint is justified, the Ombudsman will act on his behalf. The action he takes varies according to the nature of the complaint. He may gently reprimand an official, or he may even suggest to parliament that a law be altered. The following case is a typical example of the Ombudsman's work. A foreigner living in a Swedish village wrote to the Ombudsman, complaining that he had been treated unfairly by an officer simply because he was a foreigner. The Ombudsman immediately wrote to the chief of police in the district, asking him to send a record of the case. There was nothing in the record to show that the foreigner's complaint was justified, and the chief of police firmly denied the accusation. It was impossible for the Ombudsman to take action. But when he received a similar complaint from another foreigner in the same village, he immediately sent one of his lawyers to look into the matter. The lawyer ascertained that the officer had indeed treated foreigners unfairly on several occasions. The fact that the officer was prejudiced against foreigners could not be recorded in the official files. It was only possible for the Ombudsman to find this out by sending one of his representatives to check the facts. The officer in question was firmly reprimanded and was told that if any further complaints were made against him, he would be dealt with more seriously. The Ombudsman's prompt action at once put an end to an unfair practice that might otherwise have gone unnoticed.

grammar_points.name: suggest/insist/demand that + (should) + 动词原形(虚拟)
be qualified to do / be subject to / be justified
固定短语 in writing / on one's behalf / in question / put an end to
形容词后置修饰名词(complaints large and small)
so … that / it is possible for sb to do

stage5.stem: "The Ombudsman suggested that the law ___ altered."(suggest that 后从句用(should)+动词原形;此处被动,填动词原形)
stage5.stem_cn: 司法特派员建议修改这条法律。

stage5.stem: "The committee demanded that every letter ___ examined in detail."(demand that 后从句用(should)+原形;被动填原形)
stage5.stem_cn: 委员会要求每封信都详细审阅。

stage5.stem: "He insisted that the official ___ apologize to the citizen."(insist that 后从句要用哪个助动词 + 动词原形)
stage5.stem_cn: 他坚持要求那名官员向公民道歉。

stage5.stem: "The person appointed is suitably qualified ___ investigate grievances."(be qualified ___ do:胜任做,填不定式符号)
stage5.stem_cn: 被任命的人完全胜任调查冤情。

stage5.stem: "The Ombudsman is not subject ___ political pressure."(be subject ___:受…控制,填介词)
stage5.stem_cn: 司法特派员不受政治压力控制。

stage5.stem: "If a complaint is ___, the Ombudsman will act on the citizen's behalf."(be ___:有正当理由的,填过去分词)
stage5.stem_cn: 如果投诉有理,特派员就会替公民出面。

stage5.stem: "Complaints must be made in ___."(in ___:以书面形式,填名词)
stage5.stem_cn: 投诉必须以书面形式提出。

stage5.stem: "The Ombudsman acts ___ the citizen's behalf."(___ one's behalf:代表某人,填介词)
stage5.stem_cn: 司法特派员代表公民行事。

stage5.stem: "His prompt action put an ___ to the unfair practice."(put an ___ to:制止、结束,填名词)
stage5.stem_cn: 他的果断行动制止了这种不公做法。

stage5.stem: "He investigates complaints large and ___ from all levels of society."(意义相反的形容词并用,后置修饰 complaints)
stage5.stem_cn: 他调查社会各阶层大大小小的投诉。

stage5.stem: "The officer ___ question was firmly reprimanded."(“当事的、所涉及的”,___ question,置于名词后,填介词)
stage5.stem_cn: 当事的那名警官受到严厉批评。

stage5.stem: "It was a grievance ___ against the State."(过去分词后置修饰 grievance:针对…的)
stage5.stem_cn: 那是一桩针对政府的冤情。

stage5.stem: "The system worked ___ well that other countries adopted it."(“如此…以至于”,程度副词与 that 搭配)
stage5.stem_cn: 这套制度效果很好,别国也采用了。

stage5.stem: "It was impossible ___ the Ombudsman to take action."(it + 形容词 + ___ sb + to do:形式主语,填介词)
stage5.stem_cn: 司法特派员起初无法采取行动。

stage5.stem: "It was only possible for him to find out ___ sending a representative."(“通过做…”,___ + 动名词,填介词)
stage5.stem_cn: 他只有派代表去核实才能查明。

stage5.stem: "An official who is domineering and pushy is ___."(“高压的、专横的”用哪个词)
"To find out the truth for certain is to ___ it."(“查明、弄清”用哪个词)
"Someone who judges unfairly before knowing the facts is ___."(“有偏见的、不公平的”用哪个词)
stage5.stem_cn: 未了解事实就不公判断、有偏见的。
